## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode glob/grep include-after-ignore ordering SMALL ~2-3h (tools, glob, grep)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #15017 (merged 2026-10-14) applies glob and grep include patterns after ignore rules, fixing a regression where ripgrep overrides beat `.gitignore`. Commit titles: "fix(cli): stop glob and grep include patterns from bypassing .gitignore", "fix(cli): apply grep include and find globs after ignore rules". Issue: glob and grep tools allowed `include` patterns to override `.gitignore` via ripgrep's `--glob` flag, so `glob --include="node_modules/**/*.js"` returned ignored files even when `.gitignore` listed `node_modules/`. Root cause: ripgrep's `--glob` overrides (positive and negative) are evaluated AFTER default ignore rules (`--no-ignore` flag family), so a positive `--glob` can opt ignored files back in. Fix: (1) validate that `include` patterns do not conflict with ignore rules (fail early if `include` tries to bypass `.gitignore`), (2) apply include filtering in post-processing (client-side, after ripgrep returns results) instead of passing `--glob` overrides to ripgrep, (3) add tests confirming `include` respects `.gitignore` (node_modules, .git, hidden folders). PR includes test suite with ripgrep on every platform (Linux/macOS/Windows) to verify include-after-ignore ordering (L1-50 in `tests/core/glob.test.ts` placeholder reference).

- **Why**: Alexi has glob and grep tools under `src/tool/tools/glob.ts` and `src/tool/tools/grep.ts`. Check if include patterns bypass `.gitignore` or are applied after ignore rules. Kilocode issue: users passing `include` patterns expected `.gitignore` to still apply (exclude node_modules, .git), but ripgrep `--glob` overrides brought ignored files back. Alexi equivalent: (1) audit `glob.ts` and `grep.ts` for ripgrep invocation (`rg --glob` or equivalent), (2) check if `include` patterns are passed as ripgrep flags or applied client-side, (3) if ripgrep `--glob` is used, test that `include` respects `.gitignore` (create test with `node_modules/` in `.gitignore`, glob with `--include="node_modules/**/*.js"`, verify ignored files NOT returned), (4) if gap exists, apply include filtering in post-processing (filter ripgrep output by include pattern client-side, do NOT pass include as `--glob` override). SMALL ~2-3h: audit glob/grep tools for include-after-ignore ordering, add post-processing filter if ripgrep `--glob` overrides found, test include respects `.gitignore`.

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/15017 (glob/grep include-after-ignore), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/tools/glob.ts (Alexi glob tool), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/tools/grep.ts (Alexi grep tool), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/glob-ignored.ts (Alexi glob ignored allowlist)

- **Category**: tools (glob, grep, include-after-ignore ordering)

- **Size**: SMALL ~2-3h (audit glob/grep tools for ripgrep `--glob` usage, check if include bypasses `.gitignore`, add post-processing filter if needed, test include respects `.gitignore`)

#### 2. Kilocode fork-from-message MEDIUM ~4-6h (command, session)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #15004 (merged 2026-10-14) forks a remote session from a specific message. Commit title: "feat(cli): fork a remote session from a message". Feature allows users to fork a session starting from a chosen message id (mid-conversation fork), instead of forking the entire session history from the beginning. Use case: user wants to branch from a specific point in a long conversation (e.g. after message 10 of 30), exploring an alternative path without carrying the later messages. Implementation: (1) new `kilo fork --from-message <message_id>` command (or `kilo fork <session_id> --from-message <message_id>`), (2) session manager copies session up to the specified message (truncates history at that point), (3) new forked session starts with the truncated transcript, (4) original session unchanged. PR adds fork-from-message support to remote sessions (sessions stored on Kilo Hub or remote worktrees), local sessions already had fork support (fork entire session). Constraint: message id must exist in the session being forked (validated before fork, error if message not found).

- **Why**: Alexi has session forking via `/fork` command in interactive mode (`src/cli/interactive.ts` L1-500 references fork command, `src/cli/utils/completer.ts` L1-100 lists fork in session commands). Check if fork-from-message (fork starting at a specific message id) exists or if only full-session fork is supported. Kilocode feature: fork from mid-conversation, not just from session start. Alexi equivalent: (1) audit `src/core/sessionManager.ts` for fork implementation (`forkSession()` method or similar), (2) check if fork supports a `fromMessageId` parameter (truncates history at that message), (3) if only full-session fork exists, add fork-from-message support: (a) add `--from-message <message_id>` flag to fork command, (b) modify fork logic to copy session up to specified message (slice transcript array at message index), (c) validate message id exists in source session, (4) test forking from mid-conversation (create session with 10 messages, fork from message 5, verify forked session has only messages 1-5). MEDIUM ~4-6h: audit fork implementation for from-message support, add message-id parameter if missing, implement transcript truncation at fork point, test mid-conversation fork. DEFER if Alexi has no fork command at all (implement full fork first, then add from-message).

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/15004 (fork-from-message), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/sessionManager.ts (Alexi session manager), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/interactive.ts (fork command reference), git log shows no `src/cli/commands/fork.ts` (fork may be interactive-only or embedded in sessions command)

- **Category**: command (fork-from-message, session)

- **Size**: MEDIUM ~4-6h (audit fork implementation for from-message support, add `--from-message` flag if missing, implement transcript truncation at message id, test mid-conversation fork, DEFER if no fork command exists)

#### 5. Cline plugin worker-thread isolation REFERENCE-ONLY (desktop, plugins)

- **What**: Cline PR #14957 and #15034 (merged 2026-10-14) run plugins in worker threads for isolation. Commit titles: "feat(core): load plugins in the hub process and surface plugin errors", "feat(core): default a worker-thread transport for isolated plugins". Feature: (1) plugins run in worker threads (one worker per plugin per session) instead of in-process, (2) worker crash (uncaught error, process.exit) turns off that plugin without killing the host, (3) worker stdout/stderr discarded (no host stdout corruption), (4) setup context and tool context routed into workers (ctx.cwd, ctx.emitEvent, ctx.onDispose, abort signals, emitUpdate), (5) plugin status tracking (ready/degraded/failed, failure threshold, reload, `plugins.list/status/reload` commands), (6) `CLINE_PLUGIN_MODE` defaults to `worker` (opt-in `in_process` or `sandbox` via env var). #### 6. Cline undici idle timeout fix REFERENCE-ONLY (vscode, providers)

- **What**: Cline PR #15024 (merged 2026-10-14) disables undici's 5-minute idle timeout for local model providers. Commit title: "fix: stop undici's 5-minute idle timeout killing local model requests". Issue: Node's fetch uses undici with default `bodyTimeout: 300_000` (5 minutes since last byte received). Local LLM servers (LM Studio, Ollama) go silent while processing large prompts (headers arrive immediately, then no body bytes until first token generated), so requests longer than 5 minutes died mid-stream with `UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT` even though server was still generating. Fix: (1) route local model providers (LM Studio, Ollama, OpenAI Compatible on loopback/private IPs, LiteLLM on loopback) through `undici.fetch` with `headersTimeout: 0, bodyTimeout: 0` (infinite), (2) gate on base URL being local network (loopback, private/link-local/CGNAT ranges, single-label hosts, `.local`/`.internal` domains), (3) keep proxy-aware fetch for remote gateways (corporate OpenAI Compatible proxies need VS Code's `http.proxy` / OS proxy handling), (4) cancellation stays with each request's AbortSignal (no timeout = relies on manual cancel or connection drop).

- **Why**: Alexi has provider implementations under `src/providers/`, including OpenAI-compatible providers. Check if Alexi uses Node's fetch (undici) and if local model timeouts are disabled. Cline issue: local LLM requests timing out during silent generation phases (long prompt processing). Alexi equivalent: audit `src/providers/openai/` and `src/providers/http-transport.ts` for fetch calls, check if `bodyTimeout` / `headersTimeout` are disabled for local providers (localhost, 127.0.0.1, 192.168.x.x). REFERENCE-ONLY: Cline pattern shows local-network detection (loopback bypass, private IP ranges, .local/.internal domains) and selective timeout disabling (local infinite, remote keeps proxy support). If Alexi users report `UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT` or equivalent fetch timeout errors with local LLMs, reference this fix ~2-3h (add local-network check, wrap local providers with timeout-free fetch). Current priority UNKNOWN (depends on local LLM usage in Alexi).

- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/15024 (undici idle timeout fix for local models), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/openai/ (Alexi OpenAI-compatible providers), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/http-transport.ts (Alexi HTTP transport)

- **Category**: N/A (providers, local models, undici timeout, reference-only)

- **Size**: SKIP immediate work. REFERENCE - if Alexi users report fetch timeout errors with local LLMs, disable bodyTimeout for local-network providers ~2-3h.
